message: Aggregate source-presence arrays widen ResultTable row cells and mechanically require backend/src/measures/measures.service.ts compile narrowings, but that file is outside golden-provenance write_scope; extend scope or direct a serialized-string API representation.

notes: FINAL direction — the SCALAR-AGGREGATE, no-widening design (do NOT extend scope to measures.service.ts, do NOT put any array type in the ResultTable row union). Root cause of the ripple: SourcePresence[] was added to the ResultTable row value union (api.ts), breaking measures.service.ts:156,171 which persist row cells typed string|number|null. FIX: (1) REVERT the ResultTable row value union to string|number|null; keep per-row source_presence as the SCALAR  only. (2) In the composed OUTER SELECT, do NOT add any provenance column to GROUP BY (that was the grain bug). At the composed relation's natural (gl_code, month) grain each provenance value is functionally dependent on the group, so carry it with a SCALAR AGGREGATE returning that single value as a TEXT/JSON string: source_presence -> min(source_presence) AS source_presence (scalar string); budget_component_labels -> to_json aggregated to ONE json array string per group (e.g. min over the per-row jsonb array, or json_agg(DISTINCT label) if unnested) AS budget_component_labels; active batch ids -> ONE json string of the (source,period,batchId) tuples for the row's month, e.g. min() of a to_jsonb(jsonb_build_array(...)) AS active_batch_ids. All are STRING cells through PostgresAdapter (no text[] comma issue, no array in the row union). (3) SelectionExecutor JSON.parses these strings onto the typed Provenance object: the (source,period,batchId) tuple SET + the label SET (a coarser aggregate-row presence set also lives on the Provenance object, NOT the row). Fix the selectionExecutor.ts:240 ProvenanceBatch shape mismatch so the parsed tuple matches ProvenanceBatch {source,period,batchId}. (4) Update composed-relation.db.test.ts:43 destructuring for the new scalar-string provenance columns. Re-run typecheck/structural + test:hermetic + the D-0008 host proof. This keeps measures.service.ts OUT of scope entirely.

notes: AUTHORIZED, and it is my error, not yours: the repo-root .next/trace is a Next.js dev-server artifact created when a dev server was started from the repo root, and it was swept into the task commit by a 'git add -A'. The root .gitignore has no .next entry (only frontend/.gitignore ignores .next/). Delete the tracked .next/trace and add '.next/' to the ROOT .gitignore in the same change. Both files are mechanically-implied cleanup of an accidental generated artifact, not new scope, and are recorded on the stage with amend-scope.

You are right that the grain cannot be recovered from a GL/month result, and the ruling is NOT to add a query path or touch the builder/executor. RULING: change the DISPLAY GRAIN of the bucket to match the grain of the only amounts that exist. Emit ONE bucket row per unmapped GL CODE, never one per master bucket ENTRY. Fold the master's bucket entries by gl_code: costCentre stays the single cost centre when that GL has exactly one bucket entry, and is null when it has several (a GL booked across cost centres is not a triple any more, exactly as a Budget-only GL is not); provisional is true if any folded entry is provisional; reason names each folded entry's cost centre and reason so the review list still tells Srihari WHICH cost centre is wrong; actual and budget are that GL's totals from the governed result, assigned EXACTLY ONCE. This keeps the settled product decision intact (each row carries BOTH an Actual and a Budget amount, costCentre null where there is no single cost centre), keeps the gap visible rather than absorbed (decision 0018 as amended), and makes the list reconcilable against the slice totals because no amount is ever copied onto two rows. Acceptance criterion 3's word 'triples' means the reviewable identity of the gap, not a guarantee that a GL appears once per cost centre - and for today's master every unmapped GL has exactly one cost centre, so the rendered list is unchanged while the misattribution becomes impossible for any future master. Update mis-selection.controller.test.ts to prove the fold with a master where ONE GL carries TWO bucket entries: expect a single row, costCentre null, and the GL total counted once.
